newsitem.title: USA: Senate votes to confirm Barshefsky to top trade post.
newsitem.headline: Senate votes to confirm Barshefsky to top trade post.

text.p: The Senate Wednesday confirmed Charlene Barshefsky as U.S. trade representative after voting to remove a legal barrier to her taking office as President Clinton's top trade negotiator.
Barshefsky will succeed Mickey Kantor, who has moved to head the Commerce Department. She was Kantor's deputy and has been serving as acting trade representative.

Before confirming Barshefsky on a 99-1 vote, the Senate approved a waiver of a 1995 law that bars anyone who previously represented a foreign government in a trade dispute with the United States from occupying the trade post.
The waiver was needed because Barshefsky represented the Canadian lumber industry in a dispute with the United States while she was with a Washington law firm.

Sen Daniel Patrick Moynihan, a New York Democrat, told the Senate he had received a letter from President Clinton's legal counsel Charles Ruff saying that "to ensure the absolute propriety" of Barshefsky's appointment she would not take her post until waiver resolution had been enacted into law.
The waiver must be passed by the House and signed by the president.
